AND_IT_SITS_BELOW_THE_TOKEN_ITSELF.the_fork_is_named_not_picked: a single representation-native matvec sustains 160.9 GB/s while the whole token sustains 337.27. Two candidates and this block CANNOT separate them: (a) dispatches OVERLAP, which ACCELERATOR_DISPATCH_IS_NOT_THE_PRICE measured directly at +23.76% for doubled dispatches AND doubled weights rather than +100%; or (b) the resident's SHIPPED Metal kernel is ~2.1x better per-kernel than anything here. Both are live. Picking one would be the untested diagnosis this program has now written down and refuted twice.

THE_PRODUCTION_EVIDENCE_THAT_SETTLES_THE.what_bandwidth_bound_predicts: S031 s0's own frontier holds THREE bodies of the same parent at 3.1393 / 2.9802 / 2.5970 complete EBPW -- a 20.9% density range. If decode were bandwidth-bound, 17.3% fewer bytes from SEALED to CLEAN would buy +20.9% raw TPS.
THE_PRODUCTION_EVIDENCE_THAT_SETTLES_THE.what_was_recorded: 34.14 / 34.12 / 33.12 raw TPS. The 17.3% byte cut bought -3.0%, and TPS is MONOTONE THE WRONG WAY: the DENSEST body is the FASTEST, Spearman(EBPW, TPS) = +1.000 where bandwidth-bound demands -1.000.
THE_PRODUCTION_EVIDENCE_THAT_SETTLES_THE.effective_bandwidth_falls_as_bytes_fall: active 337.3 -> 318.8 -> 266.8 GB/s (complete 360.3 -> 341.9 -> 289.2). The denser body moves fewer bytes AT A LOWER RATE, so the time barely moves. That is the arithmetic-bound signature at BODY level, and it corroborates the kernel measurement above from production data S031 already recorded.
THE_PRODUCTION_EVIDENCE_THAT_SETTLES_THE.robust_to_the_one_assumption: the active figures subtract the sealed body's embedding table from all three, which assumes a comparable embed rate. The COMPLETE figures assume nothing and show the identical direction, so the finding does not rest on it.

WHAT_THIS_CORRECTS_IN_MY_OWN_PREVIOUS_BL.what_stands: the CEILING. 9.879 GB/token against a 589.73 GB/s roof still caps raw TPS at 59.70 against the 71.67 that 50 accepted TPS needs at the 30/43 floor. Fewer bytes remain NECESSARY.
WHAT_THIS_CORRECTS_IN_MY_OWN_PREVIOUS_BL.what_is_corrected: ACCELERATOR_TOKEN_BYTES_ATLAS concluded 'ONLY FEWER BYTES CAN' reach the target, which reads as SUFFICIENT. It is not. The byte lever has ALREADY BEEN PULLED IN PRODUCTION, by 17.3%, and returned -3.0% TPS. Fewer bytes are necessary and demonstrably NOT sufficient, because a denser representation costs MORE unpack arithmetic per byte and the kernels are unpack-bound at 27% of roof.
WHAT_THIS_CORRECTS_IN_MY_OWN_PREVIOUS_BL.the_amendment_is_in_place: receipts/headless/ACCELERATOR_TOKEN_BYTES_ATLAS.json carries this correction so nobody reaches the stronger reading without it.

claim_boundary: MY KERNEL IS NOT THE RESIDENT'S KERNEL. Both native arms are ws_rtn_q4_g64 at 4.25 bpw; the resident's MLP is affine_q2 group 32 at a measured 2.50 bpw, a DIFFERENT format that reads fewer bytes and does MORE unpack per byte. The direction transfers and the absolute GB/s does not.

THE 34.14 / 34.12 / 33.12 TPS FIGURES ARE RECORDED, NOT RE-MEASURED HERE, and the 3.0% gap between the fastest and slowest is small enough that it could be noise -- what is NOT noise-sized is the ABSENCE of the +20.9% a bandwidth-bound model demands.

BENCH_STATE CONTENDED throughout -- the operator's job holds 40.63 GiB at 102.1% CPU and was NOT killed (S032 s24). Every absolute GB/s is a LOWER BOUND; the RATIOS between arms measured back to back in one process carry common-mode contention and are what the block rests on.
the tpr64 arm carries 9.68% IQR, inside the 10% gate but the widest of the three; dense 6.30% and tpr1 7.68%.
ONE shape, ONE machine, ONE dtype, INSTANCE. No model was executed, no capability run, no representation graded and no adequacy claim moves.
THE GEOMETRY SWEEP IS TWO POINTS, tpr 1 and 64. Nothing between them was measured and no optimum is claimed.
next: the wall is the unpack, so the lever is an unpack that costs fewer instructions per weight -- a lookup rather than a shift-mask-subtract-multiply chain, or a format whose codes decode with less arithmetic. That is a JOINT Gravity/Accelerator question and neither front can answer it alone.

AMENDED_2026-08-26_THE_UNPACK_IS_NOT_THE.what_stands: fewer bytes are NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, and the three-body production evidence (3.1393 / 2.9802 / 2.5970 EBPW at 34.14 / 34.12 / 33.12 raw TPS) is unchanged -- and is now EXPLAINED rather than only observed.
AMENDED_2026-08-26_THE_UNPACK_IS_NOT_THE.what_is_corrected: this receipt named the UNPACK as the wall. It is not. A deletion control running the same geometry and element count with the packed array NEVER READ measures 0.2897 ms against the real kernel's 0.2825 -- reading 44.6 MB of weights costs NOTHING MEASURABLE. Removing the decode arithmetic (a 256-entry LUT, this receipt's own named lever) is 16.1% SLOWER; removing three quarters of the load instructions (4-byte words) changes nothing at 1.004x over 12 round-robin rounds. The wall is the PER-ELEMENT matvec rate -- one x read and one FMA per weight at 307.7 G elem/s -- which is neither the bytes nor the unpack.
AMENDED_2026-08-26_THE_UNPACK_IS_NOT_THE.why_the_earlier_reading_was_reachable: the comparison here was native against DENSE, and native converting only 40% of its byte ratio is consistent with an unpack cost AND with an element floor. Separating them needed a deletion control and this block did not run one.
